verdict: Avoid new iron & steel exposure in Angul for now; the data call is Avoid (27) and the local news flow does not lift it — lend only to the strongest downstream units already on our books, and only with monthly cash-flow control.
title: Angul iron & steel: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Angul is a primary-steel town first and a re-rolling town second.** The anchor is Jindal Steel's Angul plant, which management says is running at 70% utilisation and is targeted to reach 110% within twelve months [3]. Around that anchor sit secondary re-rollers, fabrication units, scrap and sponge-iron traders, and transport operators. **Cash is made on the spread between input cost (iron ore, coal, scrap, power) and finished-steel price, multiplied by tonnes sold** — not on price alone. Peer results show the split clearly: JSW Steel more than tripled September-quarter profit to Rs.5,279 crore on better volumes, higher steel prices and strong domestic demand [4], while Kirloskar Ferrous grew revenue 17% y-o-y to INR 2,046.7 crore but saw EBITDA margin fall as coking coal costs and rupee depreciation offset the growth [6]. **So when a proposal lands, check the unit's conversion spread and its power and coal contracts before you look at turnover; if the margin story rests on price alone, ask for the last six months of invoice-level realisations.**

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is weak even as the national steel cycle looks strong.** Odisha GST collections grew 0.5% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and Odisha electricity demand grew 5.1% against India's 9.5% [D] — both local stress signals. Nationally, IIP for NIC 24 (basic metals) is up only 2.4% YoY [D], and Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band [D], which raises freight and power cost for every unit in the chain. **The peer set is doing well on volume but not on margin [4][6], and that is exactly the shape that hurts small re-rollers: they sell into a firm price but buy coal and power at inflated cost.** Note that the rating reports [8][9][10][11] are undated and mostly about large or distant entities — treat them as background on sector risk, not as Angul evidence. **Sources say little specific about Angul's secondary units, so lean on first principles and the peer margin pattern.**

## Where the growth is — and who to avoid
**Pursue the service layer around the anchor's ramp-up, not the steel-makers themselves.** If Jindal Steel moves Angul from 70% to 110% utilisation [3], the beneficiaries are scrap and sponge-iron suppliers, slag and by-product handlers, in-plant logistics and maintenance contractors, and fabrication units with purchase orders from the anchor. **These borrowers have a visible counterparty, short working-capital cycles and no steel-price exposure of their own.** Avoid standalone secondary re-rollers with no tied ore or coal source, no captive power, and receivables concentrated in one or two traders — they carry the full input-cost squeeze shown in [6] with none of the scale. **If a re-roller proposal arrives, ask for the power tariff contract and the top-five customer list; if either is missing, decline.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the anchor relationship, not against the balance sheet.** Take assignment of receivables or escrow of payments from the anchor where the borrower is a contractor or supplier; keep tenor inside the work order or supply contract. **Take every month: stock and receivable statements, GST returns, electricity bills, and the anchor's payment ledger for that vendor.** Set a covenant that total outside liabilities stay within a stated multiple of net worth, and a drawing-power cap tied to verified receivables. **If the borrower cannot produce monthly GST filings that match bank credits, stop enhancement and ask for the reconciliation.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local demand gauges first.** If Odisha GST growth stays below India's for another quarter [D], treat it as a sign that end-demand in the state is not absorbing the anchor's extra output. **Watch the anchor's own utilisation disclosure [3] — if the 110% target slips, the service-layer order book thins quickly.** At the borrower level, a fall in electricity consumption per tonne produced, rising creditor days, or a shift from cash to credit sales are the first signs of a margin squeeze. **If any two of these appear in the same month, cut limits and move the account to weekly review.**
